requirement:
HC represents a GitHub issue by a stable owner, repository, and issue-number
identity. Reading the node supplies the issue's title, opening post, and
open/closed status as one snapshot. HC computes its fingerprint and formatted
text from that supplied snapshot through `Domain`.

For illustration:

```rust,ignore
struct GithubIssueContents {
    title: String,
    opening_post: String,
    status: IssueStatus,
}

enum IssueStatus {
    Open,
    Closed,
}
```
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes` has three obligations:
- A GitHub issue is represented by a stable owner, repository and issue-number identity.
- Reading the node supplies the title, opening post and open/closed status as one snapshot.
- The fingerprint and formatted text are computed from that snapshot through `Domain`.

The reference search found no `{test}` references to the requirement. The only `{test}` and `{impl}` sites in the project that mention it are none; the only reference is a `{fixme}`. The `HabeasNode` enum in `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` has no GitHub issue variant. This is the gap.

The `{fixme}` block on `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` names `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes` directly. Its body says stable owner/repository/number identity and the retained title/opening-post/status contents have no implementation or tests. That is the same missing-test gap. It names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26`, which is open, so the acknowledgment is valid.

The acknowledgment still describes a real gap, so it is not stale. Sibling `{fixme}` blocks cover the refining sub-requirements (`.inputs`, `.open`, `.related`, `.cache`) and are out of scope here.

The determination is FIXME rather than true because the tests do not cover the requirement. It is FIXME rather than false because every gap is acknowledged.
